title: 100,000 Buddhas in One Cliff, Carved for 400 Years — Longmen Grottoes | China Travel Expert
description:
One cliff face in Luoyang holds more than 100,000 hand-carved Buddhas — the work of over 400 years.

The Longmen Grottoes began in 493 AD, when the Northern Wei emperor moved his capital to Luoyang, Henan. Carving continued through seven dynasties, leaving 100,000+ statues, 2,800 inscriptions and 2,345 niches. The crown jewel is the Fengxian Temple's Vairocana Buddha — 17.14 m tall, with a head 4 m long and ears nearly 2 m each; tradition holds its serene face was modeled on Empress Wu Zetian, who helped fund it. Longmen was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

🧭 Expert Tip: Walk across to the far riverbank and look back near dusk — the whole cliff of niches is lit, and you finally see the scale in one frame.
